PRIVACY IS THE ARCHITECTURE

Your config.
Your device.

Conversion runs in JavaScript on your device. The hosted page supplies the code; your pasted configuration is not sent to a conversion service.

What we do

  • Parse strict JSON with size and nesting limits.
  • Reject reserved object keys.
  • Redact likely credential fields by default.
  • Report uncertain paths and launch commands.
  • Export only when you explicitly choose to.

What the app can access

Only text you paste and the file you select. It cannot inspect your installed apps, verify local paths, or execute an MCP server.

No configuration is saved to localStorage, IndexedDB, cookies, logs, or a backend. Reloading clears the session.

Before you run a migrated server

Read its command, check the package publisher, pin a trusted version, and restrict file access to the directories you intend to expose. An MCP server inherits permissions from the app that launches it.

Credential detection is a heuristic. Inspect the input and output yourself. Exported files and clipboard content may contain sensitive information when redaction is switched off. Browser extensions and a compromised device remain outside this app’s protection.

FROM CONVERSION TO CONNECTION

Bring it across.

A configuration is a starting point. Your target device still needs the runtimes, packages, and files it references.

01

Back up the original

Save a copy of your existing configuration. Paste strict JSON or import a file up to 256 KB.

02

Choose the destination

Enter the actual target account name. Select the original app format, or switch between mcpServers and VS Code’s servers map. Other JSON apps get path migration only.

03

Review the report

Resolve unknown drives, app-data estimates, shell commands, and host-specific variables. Replace REPLACE_LOCALLY values with credentials using the destination app’s supported secret mechanism.

04

Install, place, and verify

Install the required runtimes and trusted server packages. Check every directory exists, merge the result into the app’s configuration, then restart or reload the app and inspect server status.
